visuals: The rugged green mountains of Haiti under a bright tropical sun. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: With mountains, tropical forests, and sunny beaches, Haiti’s got it all.

visuals: A serene Haitian beach with turquoise water and palm trees swaying in the wind. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Just remember to bring an umbrella between April and October, that’s rainy season!

visuals: Dark storm clouds on the horizon over a lush Haitian tropical forest during the rainy season. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And don’t be surprised by sudden storms, hurricanes sometimes sweep through the region.

visuals: The peak of Pic la Selle in Haiti, the tallest mountain in the country, rising above a misty tropical landscape. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Now for my favorite part: Peek up at Pic la Selle! This mountain climbs over 8,700 feet into the sky, towering above the southern part of the country. Mountain goats would love it here!

visuals: Bassin Bleu in Haiti bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Speaking of symbols, meet the Hispaniolan trogon. This bird is bursting with colors, like it flew out of a paint set! It’s one of the national treasures.

visuals: A large green iguana resting on a tropical tree branch in Haiti. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And get this: Haiti is home to the giant green iguana.

visuals: A rare Hispaniolan solenodon, a small nocturnal mammal, scurrying on the forest floor in Haiti. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And the super-rare solenodon. It’s a little, insect-munching mammal found only on the island of Hispaniola. Talk about exclusive!

visuals: A busy street in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, with vibrant wall murals, colorful tap-tap buses, and a bustling open-air market. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Ever heard of Port-au-Prince? It’s the capital! You’d love strolling through its street art-covered walls and buzzing open-air markets. Who wouldn’t want to shop under the sun?

visuals: The massive Citadelle Laferrière fortress perched on a mountaintop near Cap-Haïtien, Haiti. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And check out Cap-Haïtien with its mighty mountaintop fortress, the Citadelle.

visuals: Colorful coral reefs visible through the clear turquoise water near the coast of Les Cayes, Haiti. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Or Les Cayes, where coral reefs sparkle near the shore like underwater treasure!

visuals: The Citadelle Laferrière courtyard in Haiti bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Most folks in Haiti speak Haitian Creole! Mix some French, African, and local words and boom! You’ve got a language that's full of flair! French is also used, especially in schools and government.

visuals: The vibrant streets of Jacmel in Haiti bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: About 11 million people live in Haiti, as of the early 2020s, that’s about as many people as in Georgia, USA! Pretty impressive for such a small island.

visuals: A traditional Haitian plate of griot (fried pork) served with spicy pikliz (pickled cabbage) and fried plantains. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Now let’s talk food… yum! Griot is fried pork soaked in spicy marinade and often gobbled up during family parties.

visuals: A steaming bowl of traditional Haitian joumou soup (squash soup) with beef and vegetables, served on a celebratory table. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Joumou soup! A mix of squash, beef, and veggies, is eaten every New Year’s Day to celebrate freedom.

visuals: A vibrant Haitian fruit stand under a sunny sky, piled high with ripe mangoes, bananas, and tropical fruits. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And Haiti’s fruits like mangoes and bananas are so tasty, they’re like sunshine you can eat!

visuals: Fresh Caribbean seafood being grilled over an open fire on a Haitian beach. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Seafood from the Caribbean Sea is a daily delight. Families love fresh fish.

visuals: A steaming pot of rich Haitian coffee on a rustic wooden table with green hills in the background. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And coffee from the hillsides makes sleepy mornings smell amazing.

visuals: Haitian musicians playing Kompa music with guitars and drums while people dance in a lively outdoor setting. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Time to dance! Kompa music has bouncing beats that’ll get anyone moving.

visuals: A vibrant Rara parade in the streets of Haiti with musicians playing traditional bamboo horns and drums in colorful costumes. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And Rara parades, filled with horns and drums, fill spring streets with color and cheer!

visuals: A historic illustration of the 1804 Haitian Revolution with celebratory crowds and fireworks marking independence. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Back in 1804, Haiti made world history by becoming the first country led by formerly enslaved people. That’s a huge deal, and it inspires people everywhere today.

visuals: A soccer ball on a soccer field. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: In sports news, Haiti played in the 1974 World Cup and even scored against Italy!

visuals: A portrait or action shot of historic soccer player Joe Gaetjens. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Plus, Haitian-born Joe Gaetjens made soccer headlines by scoring a goal for the U.S. in 1950. Score!

visuals: Haitian kids playing soccer with a homemade ball or grapefruit on a street in a coastal city. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Oh, and here’s a fun fact: In some communities across Haiti, including coastal cities like Les Cayes, soccer is such a big deal that you might see kids playing with a grapefruit or a homemade ball. When you don’t have a store-bought one, imagination does the job!

visuals: A portrait of the world-famous Haitian musician Wyclef Jean performing on a stage. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And music fans, listen up! Wyclef Jean, born in Haiti, went on to top global music charts and proudly supports his roots!
